_doc: The background-item estate, as DATA: every launchd agent installed on the host (and every Background Task Management row it generates) must map to a declared owner here or to a third-party exemption (Rule 55a / standard 18 §4) — anything else is UNDECLARED drift and scripts/background-items-census.py --check goes red. Origin: 2026-08-15, the operator's Login Items pane showed 'DomusAgentHost ×4' plus bare rows (bash/python3/node/cloudflared) and the estate had ZERO surface that could answer 'what are these' — the census had to be run by hand. Root cause of the display: macOS BTM names a legacy-agent row by its executable BASENAME, not the plist Label, and groups adhoc-signed binaries under a synthetic 'Unknown Developer' — so four legitimate agents sharing the DomusAgentHost TCC principal render as four identical unidentified rows. The rows are the registry's truth; the pane is a lossy projection. This file owns WHICH items are expected; spec/critical-launch-agents.json separately owns which of them must stay ALIVE. Adding a background item = ONE entry here, never a memory chore. PII-clean: labels, roles, basenames, repo paths only.

com.limen.heartbeat.role: Rule #55a one-shot heartbeat — one due read-only probe per fire, resource bounded, never resident

com.limen.creds-hydrate.role: credential organ — hydrates + verifies every secret at login and on interval

com.limen.claude-stub-heal.role: IF-GATEKEEPER-INERT effector — unregisters the unassessable vendor bundle on WatchPaths

com.ianva.gateway.role: ianva MCP doorway (lever L-IANVA-LOCAL); renders as 'bash' in Login Items

com.limen.moneta.role: MONETA sovereign mint origin (node/tsx :8787); renders as 'node'

com.limen.moneta-tunnel.role: Cloudflare tunnel fronting the mint; renders as 'cloudflared'

com.limen.mat-serve.role: private health engine (:8818, target outside this repo); renders as 'python3'

_third_party_note: Prefixes exempt under Rule 55a §4 / docs/standards/18 §4 (Apple system agents, vendor auto-updaters, Homebrew services). The standard's carve-out still applies: a misbehaving Homebrew service is treated as a Rule #55 violation and migrated to launchd-contract-wrap — the census only classifies; misbehavior belongs to launchctl status and the liveness organ.
